A_target.statement:
Let $\family {\MM_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be $\LL$-structures and $\UU$ an [[Definition:Ultrafilter on Set|ultrafilter]] on $I$.
Then for every formula $\phi$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_n \in \prod_i M_i$:
:$\displaystyle \prod_i \MM_i / \UU \models \map \phi {\sqbrk {f_1}, \ldots, \sqbrk {f_n} } \iff \set {i: \MM_i \models \map \phi {\map {f_1} i, \ldots, \map {f_n} i} } \in \UU$

B_source.statement: In the [[Definition:Henkin Construction|Henkin construction]], the truth lemma $M \models \phi \iff T^* \vdash \phi$ is proved by induction on formulas: maximal consistency handles $\neg$ and $\land$, and the Henkin witnesses handle $\exists$.

object_map.reformulation: Reuse the truth-lemma induction, with sets in the ultrafilter in place of provable sentences.

validity_conditions: Exactly one of a set and its complement lies in an ultrafilter, which handles negation.
The Axiom of Choice is used to pick witnesses in each coordinate.
proof_plan:
Proceed by induction on $\phi$.
For atomic $\phi$ this is the definition of the relations and of equality in the [[Definition:Ultraproduct|ultraproduct]], which is well-defined as $\UU$ is a filter.
For $\phi \land \psi$, the set of good coordinates is the intersection of two sets, which lies in $\UU$ {{iff}} both do.
For $\neg \phi$, the good set is the complement of that for $\phi$; as $\UU$ is an ultrafilter, exactly one of them lies in $\UU$.
